title: Maru Campos Betrays Everyone, Even the President, Morena Leader Says
author: Alejandro Páez Varela and Álvaro Delgado Gómez
content:
_This article by[Alejandro Páez Varela and Álvaro Delgado
Gómez](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/paez-delgado/) originally appeared in
the [October 23, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4892706/maru-campos-traiciona-a-todos-
incluso-a-la-presidenta-ariadna-montiel-entrevista/), an independent Mexican
digital news outlet._

_Ariadna Montiel maintained that the investigation into the "CIA Gate" should
not stop at César Jáuregui. She insisted that Governor Maru Campos must also
be tried for treason._

**Mexico City, October 23 (SinEmbargo).—** **Ariadna Montiel Reyes** ,
national president of Morena, accused the Governor of **Chihuahua** [**María
Eugenia Campos Galván**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4892554/la-gobernadora-de-
chihuahua-es-una-mitomana-responde-ariadna-montiel-a-acusaciones/) of
betraying her friends and fellow party members by holding her former state
prosecutor **César Jáuregui** responsible for the entry of Central
Intelligence Agency (CIA) agents into Mexican territory. She also accused her
of having broken the trust of President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo by revealing
details of a private conversation they had, and maintained that the state
governor should be tried for treason.

> "She is not only a traitor to the Homeland, she is a traitor to her friends,
> a traitor to her fellow party members, and she has betrayed the trust of the
> President of the Republic when she reveals a private conversation, which
> would have nothing wrong with it if that conversation had been revealed as
> an agreement but, once she made it public, the President told us this
> morning at the press conference that it was the Governor herself who turned
> in, who accused her former prosecutor as responsible for this intervention,"
> Montiel stated in an interview with Alejandro Páez and Álvaro Delgado on the
> program "**Los Periodistas** ," which is broadcast on the **SinEmbargo Al
> Aire** channel on YouTube.

On the night of October 22, Governor Maru Campos spoke with _Latinus_ about
the conversation she had with President Claudia Sheinbaum on September 19,
which was marked by mutual reproaches. Hours after that version was released,
the head of the federal Executive offered her own account of the meeting and
revealed that the PAN governor had held her former prosecutor, César Jáuregui,
responsible for the entry of CIA agents into Mexican territory and even of
illegally owning casinos.

In this regard, the Morena leader considered that the accusation against
Jáuregui did not exempt Campos Galván from her alleged responsibility for the
entry and operation of foreign agents in Chihuahua. On the contrary, she
maintained that the version presented by Sheinbaum Pardo reinforced the
questions about who had allowed the agents in and under what conditions they
had operated alongside the state police.

"What she also wants is to divert attention from something that concerns all
Mexicans, which is who is the person responsible for having allowed the entry
into national territory and operating together with the Chihuahua state
police, violating our sovereignty, who was the one who gave access to the
foreign agents… it is becoming increasingly clear that it is her, through the
institutions of the state," she maintained.

Montiel insisted that political and legal responsibility must be clarified
based on the participation of the state authorities. In that sense, she stated
that the Governor should also be tried for Treason, in addition to the
accusations faced by the former prosecutor.

> "Today Prosecutor César Jáuregui is detained for Treason, and I continue to
> affirm that the person who should also be tried for Treason is the Governor
> of the state. Today she comes out with this war of slander to try to stain
> our record. María Eugenia can keep all her accusations, but we affirm that
> we are moving forward in Chihuahua," the Morena leader stated.

flag](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-

Sheinbaum in an interview with Latinus. Photo: Facebook Maru Campos Galván

## Sheinbaum Revealed That Maru Blamed Her Former Prosecutor

In her interview with _Latinus_ , Campos described the September 19 meeting as
a "very strong, very tense" conversation, in which both officials exchanged
reproaches and raised their voices. According to her version, Sheinbaum
reproached her for the entry of US agents into Mexico, while she expressed her
disagreement with the accusations of treason that, she claimed, had been made
against her from the morning press conferences.

The Governor said that the President reproached her for having allowed the
agents to enter "through the back door" and for having created a conflict with
the United States. She also claimed that Sheinbaum mentioned three matters to
her: the presence of US agents at a drug lab, the offense of having called her
"the President of death," and the presence of US agents in the Torre
Centinela.

After that interview was released, Sheinbaum confirmed that the meeting had
been tense and offered her version of what happened. The President said that
Campos had started the conversation with complaints about the accusations of
treason and that, when talking about the entry of the foreign agents, the
Governor attributed responsibility to Jáuregui.

"When I told her: 'agents came in,' she told me: 'it wasn't me, it was my
former prosecutor.' But she didn't just tell me that, she told me they had
found corruption that the former prosecutor had committed," Sheinbaum
recounted from the National Palace.

The federal president explained that she recommended Campos file the
corresponding complaints and offered to arrange a meeting for her with the
head of the Federal Attorney General's Office (FGR), Ernestina Godoy.
According to Sheinbaum's account, the Governor later went to the Attorney
General's Office and ratified her accusations against the former prosecutor.

"I told her: 'why doesn't the Chihuahua State Attorney General's Office
proceed, and if you like I'll mention it to the Attorney General of the
Republic so she can receive you,'" the President recounted.

## "She Wants to Divert Attention"

Montiel rejected the accusations Campos had made against her and stated that
the Governor's accusations stem from her fear that the political
transformation will advance in Chihuahua. She maintained that criticism from a
PAN representative allows her to draw a distinction with the conservative
project.

"For me it is a badge of pride that a conservative like María Eugenia Campos
wants to point at us, because that allows us to differentiate ourselves from
her. I categorically deny the accusations she has made against us; at bottom
it is the fear she has that the transformation will advance in the state of
Chihuahua," she stated.

The Morena leader attributed Campos's conduct to concern over the political
and electoral landscape in the state. She maintained that the state government
had a poor approval rating and claimed that Morena was in a competitive
position against the PAN.

> She is not loyal to the homeland, nor to her friends, nor to anyone.
>
> Ariadna Montiel, president of Morena

> "Surely the people of Chihuahua will see it; her government has a very poor
> rating and Morena is well ahead of Acción Nacional. Deep down, that is what
> had her very worried, causing these kinds of outbursts and media shows, but
> that is not going to solve her problem, it is going to make it worse," she
> expressed.

Montiel accused the Governor of turning the conflict into a partisan dispute
to divert attention from the investigation into the presence of foreign agents
in Chihuahua. She also questioned the fact that Campos had publicly placed
herself on the side of Acción Nacional in the political contest, instead of
focusing on the explanations that, in her view, she owed about the conduct of
the state institutions.

"She acts as the campaign chief of the candidate Acción Nacional has decided
to back. A few days ago, when it was announced, she was wearing her PAN
T-shirt. The fear of losing the state is not about who is going to govern the
people of Chihuahua; rather, the fear is that all her corrupt dealings will be
uncovered, mainly the one that concerns us: the treason of whoever allowed our
national sovereignty to be violated," she said.

For the president of Morena, the underlying problem was not the verbal dispute
between the Governor and the President, but the need to determine who had
allowed foreign agents to enter Mexican territory and take part in operations
alongside the state police. For that reason, she insisted that Campos's
explanations about her former prosecutor's responsibility were not enough to
close the case.

Montiel maintained that Chihuahua's institutional structure was a key element
in establishing responsibility. She stated that the state Attorney General's
Office depended on the local Executive and used that argument to support her
claim that Campos had been responsible for the decisions related to the
actions of the US agents.

"The state Attorney General's Office is not autonomous as it is in the rest of
the country; the Attorney General's Office in Chihuahua depends on the state
executive, which is why we have been maintaining that **the decision for the
intervention of CIA agents in national territory was hers** ," she stated.
